fanoutqa_004310.x:
Sheldon Hackney :: Career :: chunk_0002
Hackney began his career as a lecturer in history at [Princeton University](/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University"). There, he taught in an Upward Bound program for disadvantaged students and played a role in the creation of the university's African American Studies program. While at Princeton, he moved into administration, serving as the provost from 1972 to 1975.

From 1975 to 1980, Hackney was the president of [Tulane University](/wiki/Tulane_University "Tulane University"). At Tulane, Hackney was best known for approving the November 1979 decision to tear down [Tulane Stadium](/wiki/Tulane_Stadium "Tulane Stadium"), the on-campus home of the [Green Wave football](/wiki/Tulane_Green_Wave_football "Tulane Green Wave football") team from 1926 through 1974. The Wave moved to the [Louisiana Superdome](/wiki/Louisiana_Superdome "Louisiana Superdome") upon its completion in August 1975. Tulane Stadium stood vacant for nearly five years after Tulane and the [NFL's](/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") [New Orleans Saints](/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") played their final games there, hosting high school football games and an ill-fated [ZZ Top](/wiki/ZZ_Top "ZZ Top") concert in 1976, where many fights broke out during the show.

fanoutqa_031702.x:
Hajime no Ippo :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
***Hajime no Ippo*** (はじめの一歩; lit. 'The First Step') is a Japanese [boxing](/wiki/Boxing "Boxing")-themed [manga](/wiki/Manga "Manga") series written and illustrated by [George Morikawa](/wiki/George_Morikawa "George Morikawa"). It has been serialized in [Kodansha](/wiki/Kodansha "Kodansha")'s [*shōnen* manga](/wiki/Sh%C5%8Dnen_manga "Shōnen manga") magazine *[Weekly Shōnen Magazine](/wiki/Weekly_Sh%C5%8Dnen_Magazine "Weekly Shōnen Magazine")* since October 1989, with its chapters collected in 145 *[tankōbon](/wiki/Tank%C5%8Dbon "Tankōbon")* volumes as of January 2026. It follows the story of high school student Ippo Makunouchi, as he begins his career in boxing and over time obtains many titles and defeats various opponents.

A 76-episode [anime](/wiki/Anime "Anime") adaptation produced by [Madhouse](/wiki/Madhouse_(company) "Madhouse (company)") aired on [Nippon TV](/wiki/Nippon_TV "Nippon TV") from October 2000 to March 2002. A television film and an [original video animation](/wiki/Original_video_animation "Original video animation") (OVA) were released in 2003. A second series titled *Hajime no Ippo: New Challenger* aired from January to June 2009. A third series *Hajime no Ippo: Rising* aired from October 2013 to March 2014.

In North America, the first series, including the television film, was licensed by [Geneon](/wiki/Geneon "Geneon") in 2003, which released it under the name ***Fighting Spirit***. It was re-licensed by [Discotek Media](/wiki/Discotek_Media "Discotek Media") in 2020, including the television film and the OVA.

By July 2023, the manga had over 100 million copies in circulation, making it one of the [best-selling manga series](/wiki/List_of_best-selling_manga "List of best-selling manga") of all time. In 1991, *Hajime no Ippo* won the 15th [Kodansha Manga Award](/wiki/Kodansha_Manga_Award "Kodansha Manga Award") in the *shōnen* category.

fanoutqa_027094.x:
Alcohol and cancer :: Risk factor for specific cancers :: Heavy consumption :: Endometrial cancer :: chunk_0018
Main article: [Endometrial cancer](/wiki/Endometrial_cancer "Endometrial cancer")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b5/Endometrial_adenocarcinoma_gross.jpg/250px-Endometrial_adenocarcinoma_gross.jpg)](/wiki/File:Endometrial_adenocarcinoma_gross.jpg)

An *endometrial adenocarcinoma* invading the uterine muscle

Alcohol has been identified as a risk factor for endometrial cancer.[[96]](#cite_note-96) Data however, on the association of alcohol intake and endometrial cancer is conflicting. Where data exists for an association low to moderate intake of alcohol, (less than two drinks per day) is not associated with an increased risk but an association has been suggested for higher alcohol intake.[[97]](#cite_note-97)[[98]](#cite_note-98) "Our results suggest that only alcohol consumption equivalent to 2 or more drinks per day increases risk of endometrial cancer in postmenopausal women."[[99]](#cite_note-99) "In conclusion, our results suggest that low alcohol consumption (up to one drink per day) is unlikely to substantially influence risk of endometrial cancer."[[100]](#cite_note-100)

Main article: [Gallbladder cancer](/wiki/Gallbladder_cancer "Gallbladder cancer")

Alcohol has been suggested as a risk factor for gallbladder cancer.[[101]](#cite_note-101) Evidence suggests that a high intake of alcohol is associated with gallbladder cancer.[[102]](#cite_note-102)[[103]](#cite_note-103) Men may be at a higher risk of alcohol-related gallbladder cancer than women.[[104]](#cite_note-104)

College Hall, within the 16th-century St Mary's College building

In 1410, a group of [Augustinian](/wiki/Augustinians "Augustinians") clergy, driven from the [University of Paris](/wiki/University_of_Paris "University of Paris") by the [Avignon schism](/wiki/Western_Schism "Western Schism") and from the universities of [Oxford](/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") and [Cambridge](/wiki/University_of_Cambridge "University of Cambridge") by the [Anglo-Scottish Wars](/wiki/Anglo-Scottish_Wars "Anglo-Scottish Wars"), formed a society of higher learning in St Andrews, offering courses of lectures in divinity, logic, philosophy, and law. A [charter](/wiki/Charter "Charter") of privilege was bestowed upon the society of masters and scholars by the [Bishop of St Andrews](/wiki/Archbishop_of_St_Andrews "Archbishop of St Andrews"), [Henry Wardlaw](/wiki/Henry_Wardlaw "Henry Wardlaw"),[[14]](#cite_note-Wardlaw,_Henry,_d.1440,_Bishop_of_St_Andrews-15) on 28 February 1411–12.[[15]](#cite_note-Mediaeval_university-16) Wardlaw then successfully petitioned the [Avignon Pope Benedict XIII](/wiki/Antipope_Benedict_XIII "Antipope Benedict XIII") to grant the school university status by issuing a series of [papal bulls](/wiki/Papal_bull "Papal bull"), which followed on 28 August 1413.[[16]](#cite_note-Scotland1837-17) King [James I of Scotland](/wiki/James_I_of_Scotland "James I of Scotland") confirmed the [charter](/wiki/Charter "Charter") of the university in 1432. Subsequent kings supported the university, with King [James V of Scotland](/wiki/James_V_of_Scotland "James V of Scotland") "confirming privileges of the university" in 1532.[[17]](#cite_note-St_Andrews_history_of_the_university-18)[[18]](#cite_note-19)

**Patricia Lynn Murray** ([née](/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name") **Johns**; born October 11, 1950) is an American politician serving as the [senior](/wiki/Seniority_in_the_United_States_Senate "Seniority in the United States Senate") [United States senator](/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") from [Washington](/wiki/Washington_(state) "Washington (state)"), a seat she has held since 1993. From 2023 to 2025, she held the position of [president pro tempore of the Senate](/wiki/President_pro_tempore_of_the_United_States_Senate "President pro tempore of the United States Senate"). Prior to serving in the U.S. Senate, she served in the [Washington State Senate](/wiki/Washington_State_Senate "Washington State Senate") from 1989 to 1993. She is a member of the [Democratic Party](/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)").

Born and raised in [Bothell, Washington](/wiki/Bothell,_Washington "Bothell, Washington"), Murray graduated from [Washington State University](/wiki/Washington_State_University "Washington State University") with a degree in [physical education](/wiki/Physical_education "Physical education"). She worked as a preschool teacher and later as a parenting teacher at [Shoreline Community College](/wiki/Shoreline_Community_College "Shoreline Community College"). An advocate for environmental and education issues, Murray was elected to serve on her local school board in [King County](/wiki/King_County,_Washington "King County, Washington"). The [Nobel Prizes](/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") are five separate prizes that, according to [Alfred Nobel's will](/wiki/Alfred_Nobel#Nobel_Prize "Alfred Nobel") of 1895, are awarded to "those who, during the preceding year, have conferred the greatest benefit to Mankind." Additionally, the [Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel](/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences "Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences") (often referred to as the Nobel Prize in Economics) was established by [Sveriges Riksbank](/wiki/Sveriges_Riksbank "Sveriges Riksbank") in 1968 and is awarded to a "person or persons in the field of economic sciences who have produced work of outstanding importance."

As of 2025, according to the [Nobel Foundation](/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation"),[[1]](#cite_note-nobel-awareded-women-1) 68 Nobel Prizes and the Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences have been awarded to 67 women ([Marie Curie](/wiki/Marie_Curie "Marie Curie") has been honoured twice, first in Physics in 1903, then in Chemistry in 1911).[[2]](#cite_note-2) Unique Nobel Prize laureates include 894 men, 64 women, and 27 organizations.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Main article: [Independence Day (soundtrack)](/wiki/Independence_Day_(soundtrack) "Independence Day (soundtrack)")

The [Grammy Award](/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards")-winning[[36]](#cite_note-NYTimesGrammy-36) score for the film was composed by [David Arnold](/wiki/David_Arnold "David Arnold") and recorded with an orchestra of 90, a choir of 46, "and every last ounce of stereotypical Americana he could muster for the occasion".[[37]](#cite_note-Filmtracks1997-37) The film's producer Dean Devlin commented that "you can leave it up to a Brit to write some of the most rousing and patriotic music in the history of American cinema."[[37]](#cite_note-Filmtracks1997-37) The soundtrack has received two official CD releases. [RCA](/wiki/RCA_Corporation "RCA Corporation") released a 50-minute album at the time of the film's release, then in 2010, La-La Land Records and [Fox Music](/wiki/Fox_Music "Fox Music") released a limited-edition, two-disc CD set that comprised the complete score plus 12 alternate cues.[[38]](#cite_note-38) The premiere of *Independence Day* live took place at the [Royal Albert Hall](/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall") in September 2016, with the film's score performed live for a screening of the film.[[39]](#cite_note-RAHID4live-39) This celebrated the twentieth anniversary of the film's release, and the event also featured a pre-film talk by David Arnold.

In the [1989–90 season](/wiki/1989%E2%80%9390_NBA_season "1989–90 NBA season"), Detroit lost perennial defensive forward Rick Mahorn, who was taken by the [Minnesota Timberwolves](/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") in that year's [expansion draft](/wiki/Expansion_draft "Expansion draft") and ended up on the [Philadelphia 76ers](/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") when the Pistons could not reacquire him. It was feared that the loss of Mahorn – average in talent, but high on hustle and widely considered a vital cog of the "Bad Boys" teams – would diminish the Pistons' spirit, but Rodman seamlessly took over his role.[[29]](#cite_note-1990nbafinals-29) Averaging 8.8 points and 9.7 rebounds while starting in the last 43 regular-season games, he established himself as the best defensive player in the game, lauded by the NBA "for his defense and rebounding skills, which were unparalleled in the league".[[21]](#cite_note-nbacom-21) Rodman's feats drew him his first big individual accolade: the [NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award](/wiki/NBA_Defensive_Player_of_the_Year_Award "NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award"). He also had a .595 field goal percentage, best in the league.[[22]](#cite_note-stats-22) In the [1990 playoffs](/wiki/1990_NBA_playoffs "1990 NBA playoffs"), the Pistons beat the Bulls again, and in the [1990 NBA Finals](/wiki/1990_NBA_Finals "1990 NBA Finals"), Detroit met the [Portland Trail Blazers](/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers"). [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/b/bd/MacOS_Sonoma_screenshot_with_windows.png/330px-MacOS_Sonoma_screenshot_with_windows.png)](/wiki/File:MacOS_Sonoma_screenshot_with_windows.png)

Screenshot of Sonoma

[macOS Sonoma](/wiki/MacOS_Sonoma "MacOS Sonoma") was announced during the WWDC keynote speech on June 5, 2023, and released on September 26, 2023.[[235]](#cite_note-240) macOS Sonoma revamped widgets—they can now be placed anywhere on the desktop. Game mode optimizes game performance by prioritizing gaming tasks and allocating more GPU and CPU capacity to the game, and by doing so is able to provide smoother frame rates for gameplay. The [Spotlight Search](/wiki/Spotlight_(Apple) "Spotlight (Apple)") bar and all app icons were made even more rounded, smoother animations were implemented for notifications and the lock screen, and new slow-motion screensavers of different locations worldwide were added. When logged in, they gradually slow down and become the desktop wallpaper.

**Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro**[[a]](#cite_note-9) (born 5 February 1985), nicknamed **CR7**, is a Portuguese professional [footballer](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") who plays as a [forward](/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for and [captains](/wiki/Captain_(association_football) "Captain (association football)") both [Saudi Pro League](/wiki/Saudi_Pro_League "Saudi Pro League") club [Al-Nassr](/wiki/Al-Nassr_FC "Al-Nassr FC") and the [Portugal national team](/wiki/Portugal_national_football_team "Portugal national football team"). Widely regarded as one of the greatest players in history, he has won numerous [individual accolades](/wiki/List_of_career_achievements_by_Cristiano_Ronaldo#Individual_honours "List of career achievements by Cristiano Ronaldo") throughout [his career](/wiki/Career_of_Cristiano_Ronaldo "Career of Cristiano Ronaldo"), including five [Ballon d'Ors](/wiki/Ballon_d%27Or "Ballon d'Or"), a record three [UEFA Men's Player of the Year Awards](/wiki/UEFA_Men%27s_Player_of_the_Year_Award "UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award"), and four [European Golden Shoes](/wiki/European_Golden_Shoe "European Golden Shoe"). He was also named the [world's best player](/wiki/The_Best_FIFA_Men%27s_Player#FIFA_Player_of_the_Year_(including_predecessors) "The Best FIFA Men's Player") five times by [FIFA](/wiki/FIFA "FIFA").[[note 3]](#cite_note-10) He has won [34 trophies in his career](/wiki/List_of_career_achievements_by_Cristiano_Ronaldo#Collective_awards "List of career achievements by Cristiano Ronaldo"), including five [UEFA Champions Leagues](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") and the [UEFA European Championship](/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship "UEFA European Championship").
